blocks.task_summary: Find the gradient of the tangent T_k to the curve y = h(x) at the point (k, h(k)) in terms of k, where h(x) = 15 cos(πx/50).
method_path: Apply chain rule: derivative of 15 cos(πx/50) is -15 * (π/50) * sin(πx/50)
Evaluate at x = k to get gradient: h'(k) = -(15π/50) sin(πk/50) = -(3π/10) sin(πk/50)

evidence.basis: recognition of the need to differentiate (M1); h'(x) = -15 sin(πx/50) * (π/50) = -(15π/50) sin(πx/50) = -(3π/10) sin(πx/50) A1A1; Note: Award A1 for -15 sin(πk/50) and A1 for factor of π/50.

blocks.task_summary: Given the angle between T_k and the x-axis is π/8 radians, find the possible values of k.
method_path: Recognize that gradient of tangent equals tan(angle with x-axis), but since angle is π/8 and tangent slopes downward, gradient = -tan(π/8) (or tan(7π/8))
Obtain two solutions: k ≈ 7.24 and k ≈ 42.8
accepted_alternatives: Accept k = 7.24211... and k = 42.7578... (exact from GDC)

evidence.basis: recognition that gradient of tangent = -tan(π/8) OR tan(7π/8) (M1); setting their h'(k) equal to -tan(π/8) OR tan(7π/8) (A1); k = 7.24211..., k = 42.7578...; k = 7.24, k = 42.8 A1
